title: Boot-crash evidence + release packaging: a fatal boot writes no log, and the update bundle looks launchable
description: A Discord user reported 1.2.0 flashing and closing on Windows 10 with no log anywhere. Diagnosis was blind because a fatal main-process boot error in this app is structurally unloggable, and the update-only bundle unzips into a folder that looks exactly like the app. Fix both, plus restamp the delta baselines. Targets 1.3.0.
acceptance: main.js installs uncaughtException and unhandledRejection handlers; a deliberately thrown boot error produces BOTH a visible error dialog AND a FATAL line on disk
The fatal write is synchronous - routes/logger.js appends with await and never flushes when the process is dying
The fatal log lands under the same user-data logs folder the support instructions point at, for portable and non-portable alike
Update bundle extracts to a root folder that names itself update-only, so an unzipped patch is not mistaken for the app
The update ARCHIVE filename is unchanged - shipped update scripts match it by glob and renaming it breaks in-place updates for every existing install
release-baselines for all three platforms restamped to the 1.2.0 shipped manifests so the next delta is computed against the current release, not 1.0.0
Verified: node --check on both edited files, and the fatal write path exercised at least once

attention.reason: Needs a live boot-crash smoke test (throw, confirm dialog + FATAL line, revert) and a 1.3.0 build to confirm the update-only root name and that the archive name did not drift.
